name: Neariah
overview: Neariah was a male member of the tribe of Simeon, identified specifically as the son of Ishi. His mention in Scripture is brief, focusing primarily on his tribal affiliation and lineage within the Simeonite community. There are no additional notes or significant narrative details provided about his life or actions.
namesAndTitles: The name Neariah is a proper name meaning '[young] man of y-h-v-h,' reflecting a connection to the Lord. This name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a meaningful theophoric element common in Hebrew names, highlighting a relationship to Jehovah.
familyAndRelationships: Neariah is explicitly recorded as the son of Ishi, establishing his immediate paternal lineage. Beyond this, Scripture does not provide further information about his family or other relationships.
scriptureSignificance: Neariah's significance lies primarily in his genealogical placement within the tribe of Simeon, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 4:42. His identification as the son of Ishi situates him within the broader narrative of Israel's tribal divisions and heritage. While not a prominent figure in biblical events, his inclusion helps preserve the historical record of the Simeonite lineage.
